evals.prompt: A file named storage.h contains syntax accepted by both languages, and the request does not state its consumers.
evals.expected_decision: Inspect compile commands, build targets, includers, and compatibility requirements before selecting C++, C, or both skills.
evals.expected_result: The header is changed under the actual language contracts rather than classified from its extension.
evals.expected_output: Name the classification evidence and compilation checks for every supported consumer language.

evals.prompt: A method returns string_view derived from a local std::string and callers retain the result.
evals.expected_decision: Change ownership or return representation so the view cannot outlive its owner; do not rely on const or documentation alone.
evals.expected_result: Callers receive an owning value or a view whose owner demonstrably outlives every supported use.
evals.expected_output: State the ownership/lifetime contract and tests covering retention and invalidation.

evals.prompt: Two functions currently pass a raw pointer, and a reviewer suggests replacing every pointer with shared_ptr.
evals.expected_decision: Map the ownership graph and choose value, reference, raw non-owner, unique ownership, or shared lifetime from actual retention needs.
evals.expected_result: Ownership is explicit without unnecessary heap allocation, reference counting, or hidden lifetime extension.
evals.expected_output: Explain the chosen owner and observer roles rather than applying a mechanical smart-pointer rule.

evals.prompt: Tighten a concept on a public function template used by downstream code and move its definition into a source file.
evals.expected_decision: Review source compatibility, overload resolution, available instantiations, linkage, and the project's explicit-instantiation strategy.
evals.expected_result: Supported downstream types still instantiate and link, or the compatibility change is made explicit and versioned.
evals.expected_output: Name the template/linkage contract and consumer builds used as evidence.

evals.prompt: Mark a move constructor noexcept to improve container behavior, although one called operation can throw under the current allocator policy.
evals.expected_decision: Treat noexcept as a semantic guarantee; either make the implementation truly non-throwing or leave the declaration consistent with reality.
evals.expected_result: The move path cannot unexpectedly terminate from a false noexcept promise.
evals.expected_output: Explain the exception contract, container tradeoff, and construction/move failure tests.

evals.prompt: A C++ service detaches std::thread workers that capture this; its destructor sets an unsynchronized bool and destroys the condition variable and queue while workers may still use them.
evals.expected_decision: Give workers an owning RAII lifecycle, protect the stop/queue predicate coherently, wake waiters, prevent new work, and join completion before destroying observed state; define how startup and worker failures reach the owner.
evals.expected_result: No data race, detached lifetime escape, blocked waiter, or teardown use-after-free remains, and shutdown behavior for pending work is explicit.
evals.expected_output: State ownership, synchronization, lock scope, shutdown order, failure propagation, and deterministic coordination or supported ThreadSanitizer evidence.

evals.prompt: A C++ client schedules asynchronous jobs while another thread closes it. A job can start before jobs_.push_back succeeds, that push can throw, and the public header is ABI-governed.
evals.expected_decision: Define one submit/close admission boundary, make registration and in-flight accounting exception-safe, cancel and observe any started-but-unregistered job, and preserve the governed header/ABI through implementation-owned state.
evals.expected_result: Close rejects later work, waits every admitted operation, cannot hang on failed registration, and does not trade the lifecycle fix for public layout churn.
evals.expected_output: State the linearization point, rollback/terminal path, ownership of started work, public-boundary strategy, and deterministic failure-injection plus consumer evidence.

evals.prompt: A C++ report builder calls std::async(std::launch::async, ...) for three independent blocking lookups without keeping the returned futures, then reads results the lookups write into shared member fields. Reports take the sum of the three lookup times, and a reviewer suspects a race.
evals.expected_decision: Keep each future and collect its result through get(), so the lookups overlap and their values and exceptions reach the builder instead of shared fields, or use the repository executor with the same ownership.
evals.expected_result: The lookups run concurrently, report time approaches the slowest lookup, no shared field is written concurrently, and an exception from any lookup reaches the caller with the lookup it came from.
evals.expected_output: Explain the destructor behavior that serialized the work, the ownership of each future, exception propagation, and the deterministic tests or ThreadSanitizer evidence used.
